def-linear-regression-objectives:
## Definition

Let $n,p\ge1$, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ be a fixed design matrix, let $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $\beta\in\mathbb R^p$. The empirical squared loss is

$$\ell_n(\beta)=\frac{1}{2n}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2.$$

Ordinary least squares minimizes $\ell_n(\beta)$ over $\mathbb R^p$. For $\lambda>0$, the ridge (Tikhonov) objective is

$$J^{\mathrm{ridge}}_\lambda(\beta)=\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2.$$

For $\lambda>0$, the lasso objective in the empirical-loss convention is

$$J^{\mathrm{lasso}}_\lambda(\beta)=\ell_n(\beta)+\lambda\|\beta\|_1,\qquad \|\beta\|_1=\sum_{j=1}^p|\beta_j|.$$

This lasso has the same minimizers as $n^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+2\lambda\|\beta\|_1$, the fixed-design convention with penalty parameter $\tau=\lambda$.

For a partition $G_1,\ldots,G_m$ of $\{1,\ldots,p\}$ and fixed weights $w_g>0$, the group-lasso objective is

$$J^{\mathrm{group}}_{\lambda}(\beta)=\ell_n(\beta)+\lambda\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2.$$

For a fixed matrix $D\in\mathbb R^{q\times p}$ and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0$, a fused-lasso objective is

$$J^{\mathrm{fused}}_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\beta)=\ell_n(\beta)+\lambda_1\|\beta\|_1+\lambda_2\|D\beta\|_1.$$

These group and fused formulas define objectives only; no existence, uniqueness, or algorithm guarantee is asserted for them here. The formulas use the displayed feature scales, so rescaling a column changes the penalty unless its coefficient and penalty weight are adjusted. If an intercept is included, write $X=[\mathbf 1\;X_0]$ and $\beta=(\beta_0,\gamma)$, define the loss by $\|y-\beta_0\mathbf1-X_0\gamma\|_2^2/(2n)$, partition only the coordinates of $\gamma$, and use a fused matrix of the form $D=[0\;D_0]$. Each penalty then acts only on $\gamma$ and the intercept coordinate $\beta_0$ is unpenalized.
lem-gaussian-sample-covariance-operator-:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d_k,n_k\ge1$ be integer sequences with $d_k/n_k\to0$. For each $k$, let $G_k\in\mathbb R^{n_k\times d_k}$ have mutually independent $N(0,1)$ entries. Then

$$\left\|\frac{G_k^{\mathsf T}G_k}{n_k}-I_{d_k}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow[k\to\infty]{\mathbb P}0.$$
lem-chi-square-degree-ratio:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $r_k,n_k$ be positive integers with $n_k\to\infty$ and $r_k/n_k\to1$. For each $k$, let $Z_{k,1},\ldots,Z_{k,r_k}$ be independent $N(0,1)$ random variables and set $D_k=\sum_{j=1}^{r_k}Z_{k,j}^2$. Then $D_k/n_k\to1$ in probability.
lem-finite-gaussian-max-comparison:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $m\ge2$, and let $X,Y\in\mathbb R^m$ be independent, centered Gaussian vectors with finite covariance matrices. If

$$\mathbb E[(X_i-X_j)^2]\ge\mathbb E[(Y_i-Y_j)^2]\qquad(i,j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}),$$

then $\mathbb E[\max_iX_i]\ge\mathbb E[\max_iY_i]$.
lem-standard-gaussian-maximum-expectatio:
## Statement

Assume AC. There is an integer $m_0$ such that for every $m\ge m_0$ and independent standard-normal random variables $G_1,\ldots,G_m$,
$$\mathbb E\max_{1\le i\le m}G_i\ge\frac14\sqrt{\log m}.$$
fs-wainwright-lower-signed-support-thres:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Wainwright's planned lower-threshold claim is the following: along a sequence of real Gaussian linear models with $S=\{j:\beta_j^*\ne0\}$, $s=|S|$, $N=p-s$, $s,n-s,N\to\infty$, and independent observations
$$y_i=x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta^*+w_i,\qquad x_i\sim N_p(0,\Sigma),\quad w_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2),$$
where $X$ has rows $x_i^{\mathsf T}$, $y=(y_i)$, design and noise are independent, there is no separate intercept, and $\Sigma$ has unit diagonal. Suppose constants $C_{\min}>0$, $C_{\max}<\infty$, $D_{\max}<\infty$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$ satisfy
$$\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{SS})\ge C_{\min},\qquad \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)\le C_{\max},\qquad \|(\Sigma_{SS})^{-1}\|_\infty\le D_{\max},\qquad \|\Sigma_{S^cS}(\Sigma_{SS})^{-1}\|_\infty\le1-\epsilon,$$
with $\|M\|_\infty=\max_i\sum_j|M_{ij}|$. Define
$$\theta_\ell=\frac{\bigl(\sqrt{C_{\max}}-\sqrt{C_{\max}-1/C_{\max}}\bigr)^2}{C_{\max}(2-\epsilon)^2}.$$
For every fixed $\nu>0$ and every positive non-increasing sequence $\lambda_n$, if $n<2(\theta_\ell-\nu)s\log N+s+1$, then the probability that there exists an optimizer with $\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat\beta)=\operatorname{sgn}(\beta^*)$ for $\|y-X\beta\|_2^2/(2n)+\lambda_n\|\beta\|_1$ tends to zero.
thm-ols-and-ridge-solutions:
## Statement

Let $n,p\ge1$, $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, and $y\in\mathbb R^n$. The ordinary least-squares minimizers of $\|y-X\beta\|_2^2$ are exactly the solutions of $X^{\mathsf T}X\beta=X^{\mathsf T}y$; if $\beta_0$ is one such solution, the full minimizer set is $\beta_0+\ker X$. It is a singleton if and only if the columns of $X$ are linearly independent. For every $\lambda>0$, the ridge objective $\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2$ has the unique minimizer
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{ridge}}=(X^{\mathsf T}X+\lambda I_p)^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}y.$$
lem-orthonormal-lasso-soft-thresholding:
## Statement

Let $n,p\ge1$, $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ satisfy $X^{\mathsf T}X=I_p$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\lambda>0$. The objective
$$\frac{1}{2n}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_1$$
has the unique minimizer $\widehat\beta_j=S_{n\lambda}((X^{\mathsf T}y)_j)$, where $S_a(t)=\operatorname{sgn}(t)(|t|-a)_+$, $(u)_+=\max\{u,0\}$, and $\operatorname{sgn}(0)=0$. Thus the threshold is $n\lambda$ under this loss normalization.
lem-lasso-active-set-stationarity:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $y\in\mathbb R^n$, $\lambda>0$, and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}$ be nonempty. Assume the active design $X_S$ has full column rank. If an optimizer $\widehat\beta$ of $\|y-X\beta\|_2^2/(2n)+\lambda\|\beta\|_1$ has support exactly $S$ and sign vector $b=\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat\beta_S)\in\{-1,1\}^{|S|}$, then
$$\widehat\beta_S=(X_S^{\mathsf T}X_S/n)^{-1}(X_S^{\mathsf T}y/n-\lambda b).$$
This is a necessary active-coordinate condition only; it does not assert that the candidate satisfies any inactive-coordinate condition.
fs-wainwright-signed-support-threshold-c:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice, and countable choice. Wainwright's 2006 two-sided threshold claim is the following: consider a sequence of real Gaussian linear models with $S=\{j:\beta_j^*\ne0\}$, $s=|S|$, $N=p-s$, $\rho_n=\min_{j\in S}|\beta_j^*|$, $s,n-s,N\to\infty$, and
$$y_i=x_i^{\mathsf T}\beta^*+w_i,\qquad x_i\sim N_p(0,\Sigma),\quad w_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2),$$
where observations are independent, design and noise are independent, there is no separate intercept, and $\Sigma$ has unit diagonal. Suppose constants $C_{\min}>0$, $C_{\max}<\infty$, $D_{\max}<\infty$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$ satisfy
$$\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{SS})\ge C_{\min},\quad \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)\le C_{\max},\quad \|(\Sigma_{SS})^{-1}\|_\infty\le D_{\max},\quad \|\Sigma_{S^cS}(\Sigma_{SS})^{-1}\|_\infty\le1-\epsilon,$$
where $\|M\|_\infty=\max_i\sum_j|M_{ij}|$. Define
$$\theta_\ell=\frac{\bigl(\sqrt{C_{\max}}-\sqrt{C_{\max}-1/C_{\max}}\bigr)^2}{C_{\max}(2-\epsilon)^2},\qquad \theta_u=\frac{C_{\max}}{\epsilon^2C_{\min}}.$$
Let $X$ have rows $x_i^{\mathsf T}$, $w=(w_i)$, and $y=(y_i)$. For $\lambda_n>0$, let success mean that there exists an optimizer with $\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat\beta)=\operatorname{sgn}(\beta^*)$ for the objective $\|y-X\beta\|_2^2/(2n)+\lambda_n\|\beta\|_1$. The threshold claim is that for every fixed $\nu>0$, success probability tends to zero if $n<2(\theta_\ell-\nu)s\log N+s+1$ for every non-increasing positive $\lambda_n$, and tends to one if $n>2(\theta_u+\nu)s\log N+s$, $\lambda_n\to0$, $n\lambda_n^2/\log N\to\infty$, and $\rho_n^{-1}(\lambda_n+\sqrt{\log s/n})\to0$.
